clinician.final_diagnosis: a patient with atypical chilblain-like lesions with prominent haemorrhagic bullae associated with COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 27-year-old woman presented with a 2-day history of bilateral, progressively oedematous and pruritic toes with multiple non-haemorrhagic bullae and widespread erythema. She had a prior history of ageusia and anosmia 6 weeks earlier. Two days after initial presentation, the bullae became haemorrhagic. Subsequent SARS-CoV-2 testing was positive. At a 3-month follow-up, the acral oedema and pruritus had completely resolved, and the bullous lesions healed with residual scaling and violaceous hyperpigmentation. No specific treatment was documented.
